meta.title: Backroom — Grow your business. Without doing it all yourself.
meta.description: An AI team that works with your business context: it prepares offers, research and drafts for X, Instagram and YouTube. In early access.

one.a: For founders, independent professionals with their own offer and small teams who want to build, launch or grow a business. It’s especially relevant if you have something real in the works and research, creation and distribution still depend on you.

two.q: What if I only have an idea?
two.a: You can start there, too. Your first piece of work might be understanding the problem, testing an offer or preparing a small experiment. You don’t need to pretend you already have customers; hypotheses should remain hypotheses.

three.q: How is this different from an AI chat?
three.a: A chat answers what you ask. Backroom starts from what it already knows about your business, works with a method — what to research, what to prepare, how to take in your corrections — and leaves results you can open and ask to change. What you correct once, the whole team uses.

four.q: Does it publish on X, Instagram and YouTube for me?
four.a: Not yet. Today Backroom prepares drafts and you decide where and when to publish them. Publishing from Backroom will come later and will ask for your permission on each piece.

five.a: We’re preparing early access. Leave your email and tell us what you want to move forward. We’ll contact you when we can offer you access; submitting the form does not yet create an account or guarantee a date. In our private build you can already talk with your team, open results and ask for changes, correct the shared memory and use your own AI account. Missions, For you and weekly work are being built. Connecting your channels, publishing and measuring come after that.

six.a: We haven’t published prices yet. Requesting access needs no card and starts no subscription. To use it you’ll work with your own AI account; if that plan is paid, its cost is separate and yours to manage. You’ll know the terms before deciding whether to use the product.

seven.q: What happens to my business information?
seven.a: What you decide is kept in your business’s memory: you can read and correct it, and each business has its own. Conversations are processed through your own AI account, under that provider’s terms. Publishing or reading private data on your behalf will always ask for your authorisation. Before you start we’ll explain what is stored and how to delete it; meanwhile, the <privacy>privacy policy</privacy> covers what we do with what you send in the access form.

artifacts.imageAlt: Soma identity concept: a cup, packaging and menu in cobalt blue on pale stone.

offer.title: An identity for your next café
offer.body: A Norte proposal to turn the character of an independent café into a recognisable identity.
offer.textOne: People preparing to open an independent café who need their brand to feel consistent from day one.
offer.textTwo: Visual direction, identity and initial applications for menus and packaging. Interior design and production are agreed separately.
offer.textThree: What they need ready for opening, who decides on the design and what they struggle to solve with existing alternatives.
offer.takeaway: Next step: discuss scope and priorities in a first conversation.

website.title: A page for Norte’s offer
website.body: The same proposition, turned into a simple page that opens a conversation.
website.textOne: A place of your own. A brand of your own. Visual identity for independent cafés preparing to open.
website.textTwo: A visual direction and its first applications: identity, menus and packaging. A coherent project with a scope agreed before work begins.
website.textThree: Tell us about the café you have in mind, what you’ve prepared and what you need to open. We’ll shape the proposal from there.
website.takeaway: The page illustrates an offer; its form is not connected to a real studio.

content.title: One identity. Three conversations.
content.body: The Soma concept shows how Norte works. Each format reveals a different angle of the same project.
content.textOne: One observation and three images: how the cup, menu and packaging share the same idea. Explaining the thinking invites a conversation about design.
content.textTwo: A reel that starts with a detail and reveals the whole. The visual story moves from concept to applications, without inventing a client or a success story.
content.textThree: A walk through the project: audience, references, decisions and result. Showing what was ruled out also helps explain the work.
content.takeaway: Drafts to review. Publishing from Backroom isn’t available yet.

research.title: The questions before the launch
research.body: A starting point for researching Norte’s offer. References provide direction; hypotheses need testing.
research.textOne: A design portfolio, a proposed audience and an initial scope: identity, menus and packaging for independent cafés.
research.labelTwo: WHAT WE STILL NEED TO LEARN
research.textTwo: How they choose a studio, what budget and timeline they work with and which materials take the most effort before opening. These are questions, not verified market data.
research.textThree: Show a short proposal to potential clients and listen to what they need, what they don’t understand and how they would solve it without Norte.
research.takeaway: There is no validated demand or invented customer evidence in this example.
